# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-12 (Extended v106)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 3)**: (1) Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon (Friends of the A B C meeting); le Petit-Picpus convent district (Valjean, Cosette sanctuary); M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district—Marius's attic cabinet); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière (M. Mabeuf's cottage); (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton). **Environmental conditions (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: rain threatened but held off; wind off water with salt/tar smell; roads rutted and puddled after thaw; light went early; smoke lay flat; frost silvered hedges; children chased hoop; cart loaded with turnips creaked past; chalk sun on forge wall; baker's boy late; line at oven grew long; dog barked at nothing; bell for vespers rang thinly; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage.

## Primary Locations
**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus; convent complex with garden, chapel, burial vault. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire in Marais. **CAFÉ MUSAIN**: Near Panthéon, Rue Saint-Michel; headquarters Friends of the A B C; back room with argand lamp, two windows, private stairway on Rue des Grès. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet rented for 30 francs annually. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; thatched cottage rented for fifty crowns yearly; three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge with well. **Other Paris locations**: Quai des Orfévres (engraver); Saint-Sulpice Chapel; Place Saint-Michel; Rue Saint-Jacques; Rousseau's restaurant opposite Basset's stamp-dealer, corner Rue des Mathurins; Place du Panthéon; Champs-de-Mars; Luxembourg; Invalides; Quai Malplaquet; courtyard of the Louvre; outer boulevards.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete—meditations on grace, humility, prayer. Cosette became convent scholar; thinks herself his daughter; adores him. Fauchelevent remains sole ally aware of full presence; grateful, talkative peasant of Picardy. Nuns do not suspect.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. Investigated child abduction memory; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at door. Valjean foiled spy by silence. Old woman warned Javert lodger intended to leave; Javert waited with two men at night. Valjean escaped via cut street lantern rope (Mouffetard); Javert followed from tree to tree but did not arrest hastily. **Current status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades; sure convict could not be far off.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development Continued

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years since left grandfather M. Gillenormand.

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction: "The Emperor made me a Baron...my son shall take it and bear it." Also: "At Waterloo, sergeant Thénardier saved my life...If my son meets him, he will do all the good he can." Lost medallion of black shagreen containing colonel's paper fell on attic staircase during move; never found. Marius convinced grandfather burned it; knew few lines by heart.

**Political and spiritual transformation**: Converted from childhood royalism to passionate Bonapartism; became thoroughgoing revolutionist, profoundly democratic and republican. **Recent change (Winter Year 3)**: Political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 assisted calming him. No longer held firm opinions but rather sympathies. Belonged to party of humanity; chose France from humanity, people from nation, woman from people. Pity directed to woman above all. Now preferred idea to deed, poet to hero; admired book Job more than event Marengo. When meditating on boulevards at evening, catching glimpse through tree branches of fathomless space, mystery, all that human seemed very pretty to him.

**Material condition (Winter Year 3)**: Occupied Gorbeau house cabinet (attic den minus fireplace) for 30 francs annually. Gave 3 francs monthly to old principal tenant for sweeping and bringing hot water every morning, fresh egg, penny roll. Breakfast: 2-4 sous. Dinner: 16 sous (meat, vegetables, dessert, bread, waiter). Daily food cost: 20 sous (365 francs yearly). Clothing: 100 francs. Linen and washing: 100 francs. Total sustenance: 450 francs. Had no fireplace. Wardrobe: Two complete black suits—one old "for every day," one brand new for special occasions. Three shirts total: one worn, one in commode, one at washerwoman's.

**Legal and professional status (Winter Year 3)**: Admitted to law practice despite poverty. Drew about seven hundred francs yearly from work. Learned German and English; thanks to Courfeyrac, put in communication with publisher friend; filled modest post in publishing house literature. Drew up prospectuses, translated newspapers, annotated editions, compiled biographies. Although lawyer, not practising; meditation turned him aside from pleading. Obscure and ill-paid publishing establishment came to mean sure source of work not involving too much labor; sufficed for wants.

**Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: Publisher M. Magimel offered to lodge him well, furnish regular occupation, give fifteen hundred francs year. Marius refused: accepting would renounce liberty, become hired man of letters—position would become both better and worse, acquiring comfort while losing dignity.

**Philosophy of leisure and dreams (Winter Year 3)**: After succeeding in earning living with approach to certainty, stopped, thinking it good to be poor, retrencing time from work to give to thought. Sometimes passed entire days in meditation. Multiplied plans, combinations, scaffoldings, projects for future. In this state of reverie, soul's purity would dazzle eye. Dreams reveal true character more surely than thoughts; dreams utterly spontaneous, take form of spirit even in ideal. Nothing proceeds more directly from soul's depth than unpremeditated, boundless aspirations towards destiny's splendors. Real character found in aspirations more than deliberate ideas. Each dreams of unknown and impossible according to his nature.

**Pleasures (Winter Year 3)**: Took long walks alone on outer boulevards, Champs-de-Mars, least frequented alleys of Luxembourg. Often spent half a day gazing at market garden, beds of lettuce, chickens on dung-heap, horse turning water-wheel. Passers-by stared in surprise; some thought his attire suspicious and mien sinister. Attended occasional evening parties at homes of father's old generals (Comte Pajol, General Bellavesne, General Fririon, Invalides) when invited to hear talk of his father. Put on new coat for such evenings but attended only on freezing cold days, as he could not afford carriage and would not arrive with boots otherwise than like mirrors.

**Quarrel with grandfather (Autumn Year 3)**: Violent quarrel three years ago; remained on same terms without attempting to approach each other—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's concealed suffering locked within breast; when asked about Marius, replied with sigh that he was sad case; if appearing gay, gave fillip to cuff: "Monsieur le Baron de Pontmercy is practising pettifogging in some corner or other."

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C (Winter Year 3)**: Met Courfeyrac (young friend) at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends in few days. Courfeyrac introduced Marius to Café Musain, whispered: "I must give you your entry to the revolution." Presented him as "A pupil." Due to taste for remaining outside everything, did not enter decidedly into group presided over by Enjolras. Remained good friends; ready to assist each other on occasion in every possible way; nothing more. One old friend: **M. Mabeuf**. Inclined more to old man. Owed to him revolution which took place within him; indebted for having known and loved father. "He operated on me for a cataract," Marius said.

## M. Mabeuf

**Character and occupation**: Ecclesiastic, botanist, editor, man of books and flowers. **Influence on Marius**: Marius owed to him revolution within him; indebted for having known and loved his father.

**Servant—Mother Plutarque (Winter Year 3)**: Sort of innocent spinster. Her cat Sultan filled her heart and sufficed for quantity of passion existing in her. Never proceeded further than cat. Like him, had moustache. Glory consisted in caps, always white. Passed Sundays after mass counting linen in chest, spreading dresses in piece she bought never had made up. Knew how to read. M. Mabeuf had nicknamed her Mother Plutarque.

**Relocation and new residence (Winter Year 3)**: Carried off _Flora_, copper-plates, herbariums, portfolios, books; established himself near Salpêtrière in sort of thatched cottage village of Austerlitz. For fifty crowns year got three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge containing well. Took advantage of removal to sell off nearly all furniture. Day of entrance into new quarters very gay; drove nails for engravings and herbariums with own hands, dug in garden rest of day. At night, perceiving Mother Plutarque had melancholy air and was very thoughtful, tapped her on shoulder and said with smile: "We have the indigo!"

**Philosophical disposition (Winter Year 3)**: Brains absorbed in wisdom or folly (or both) slowly accessible to things of actual life. Results in passivity resembling philosophy. Always ends in awakening but awakening tardy. Habits of mind had regular swing of pendulum. Once mounted on illusion, went very long time even after illusion disappeared. Remained puerilely but profoundly serene athwart cloud formed about him when all hopes extinguished one after another.

**Recent pleasure (Winter Year 3)**: Mother Plutarque reading romance aloud ("Bouddha and the Dragon"). M. Mabeuf struck in with low voice about dragon spouting flame from cave depths, consuming stars, having claws of tiger; Bouddha went into den and succeeded in converting dragon. Called it good book, most beautiful legend in existence.

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Context (Autumn Year 3)**: Revolutionary quiver vaguely current; breaths from '89 and '93 in air. Youth moulting; people undergoing transformation. At Paris existed Friends of the A B C.

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—the _Abaissé_,—the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Not numerous; secret society in embryonic state, almost coterie. Old map of France under Republic nailed to wall.

**Meetings (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Convened back room Café Musain; argand lamp lighted. Nearly all haranguing at haphazard; tossed words, caught up in turn; chattering in quarters. Peaceable tumults—game and uproar as much as conversation.

**Members**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students, cordial with working classes. **Grantaire**: Sceptic; lived with irony; "There is but one certainty, my full glass." Sneered at all devotion; disdained Enjolras as unaccepted Pylades yet ever returning.

## English Provincial Towns (Updated)

**Population movements**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead for Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton. **Births (Dunstead)**: Son Ferald Stenworth and daughter Isvie Stenworth born to Luwyn Brackick. **New individuals and activities (Winter Year 3)**: Rozek Stenenridge told Luena Stenenridge "You look tired"; Luena did not deny it. Luena laughed at story nobody else found funny. Luena spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Luena pressed oak lantern into Rozek's hands, would take nothing for it. In Ostcombe: Isric Thornmere mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Vesmira Thornmere and Wenelle Lindmere talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Luvie complained of aching back, as usual. **Claims and rumors**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (claim). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body seen). **Observations**: Rorald Lindmere gave Gadan Corrley solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Ravenmere. Gadan Corrley counted coins twice, came up penny short. Gadan walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Kassa remarked "I heard river is up again"; Yera Haskick said it always was in spring. **Prior rumors**: Granary fire set on purpose (rumor). Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood.

## Current Events (Winter Year 3)

**Paris student assembly**: Students of schools of law and medicine summoned to assemble Place du Panthéon at midday to deliberate on artillery of National Guard—conflict between Minister of War and "citizen's militia" over cannon parked in courtyard of Louvre. **M. Gillenormand's rage**: Read announcement in Royalist sheet; flew into rage; denounced students as "pack of brats," "urchins," "returned convicts and released galley-slaves," Republicans forming "one nose and one handkerchief" with galley-slaves. Invoked Carnot, Fouché, Sieyès as examples of Republican perfidy. Called progress madness, humanity dream, revolution crime, republic monster. **New scheming (Winter Year 3)**: Aunt Gillenormand had plotted to have Lieutenant Théodule (nephew in lancer regiment come to perform garrison duty in Paris) take Marius' place in household. Théodule entered clad in plain clothes as bourgeois, discreetly introduced; had reasoned: "The old druid has not sunk all his money in a life pension. It is well to disguise one's self as a civilian from time to time." M. Gillenormand, indulging in painful dream before Théodule's entrance, thought no more of his grandnephew after reading, merely some "Théodule or other."
